order-alerts.text: Chioma sees one of our ads and orders a sofa cover on the landing page.
Her order is placed. Every order is paid on delivery.
It arrives as an email in our Gmail inbox. Before, it could sit there unseen for up to two hours.
Every 15 minutes, Zapier checks the inbox for new emails that match the order search.
Only real orders match. Newsletters and other emails are ignored.
The order details go straight into a WhatsApp message.
Within 15 minutes of the order, my partner has it on WhatsApp, with everything needed to call her.
He calls Chioma to confirm while she’s still keen to buy.
From a new order to WhatsApp in 15 minutes, not two hours.

order-extraction.text: Over a thousand past orders sat in our Gmail inbox, one email each, with no customer list.
Each product had its own order form, so no two emails looked quite the same.
One run of the backfill workflow in n8n starts the job.
It pulls every past order email from Gmail.
It reads the orders already in the sheet
and skips them, so no order can ever be logged twice.
Then it works through the orders in paced batches.
Each email goes to the order reader, a separate workflow.
The AI, Llama 3.1 running on Groq, reads the email for meaning, wherever each detail sits.
An order is only kept if it has a usable phone number. This one does.
For bundles, the real quantity comes from the price table, not a guess.
The pieces come together as one clean order.
Back in the backfill, it paces itself, then writes the order, keyed to its Gmail ID.
Order after order, the sheet fills up: all one thousand, one hundred and forty-five, in a single day.
Orders that fail the checks, and duplicates, go to the Invalid tab with the reason. Nothing is lost.
From a buried inbox to a customer list we can sell to.

voice-receptionist.text: Ada calls the clinic to book a cleaning.
The AI receptionist answers straight away, and asks what she needs.
The agent asks the workflow for open times. A switch sends it down the availability path.
A sheet points it to the Abuja branch’s own calendar, and it reads that day’s bookings.
It finds the free one-hour slots, never the lunch hour, and sends back the first three.
Ada picks 5pm, and the agent reads her name and number back to check them.
Meanwhile, someone at the clinic books 5pm for another patient.
Before booking, the workflow checks 5pm again. It has just been taken.
So it finds three new times and sends those back instead.
The agent tells Ada 5pm has gone and offers the new times.
4pm is still free, so the booking goes into the Abuja calendar.
The agent confirms on the call. A short while later, a text goes out through Termii.
The booking sits in the Abuja calendar, with her name, number and the reason for the visit.
Ada gets a text with the branch, date and time.
Every call answered, every booking in the right branch’s diary.

whatsapp-receipts.text: Tunde, a driver, buys fuel and gets a paper receipt.
He opens the company’s WhatsApp chat and snaps a photo of it.
He sends the photo. That’s all he has to do.
The photo reaches the workflow in n8n, and it starts.
It checks the message is a photo or a PDF before going any further.
The receipt file is downloaded from WhatsApp.
Photos and PDFs are read differently. This one is a photo.
AI reads the vendor, date, total, tax and category, and flags anything it isn’t sure of.
The sender’s number is matched to the driver list in Airtable.
His name is attached. An unknown number would be saved as Unknown Driver, never dropped.
The reading and the driver are put together as one record.
Every field was read clearly, so it carries on. An unclear receipt would go to a review log instead.
It looks for this month’s folder in Google Drive.
The folder already exists, so no duplicate is made.
The receipt is pointed at the October 2026 folder.
The photo is uploaded, named by date, vendor and driver.
In Google Drive, it lands in October 2026, easy to find without opening it.
Next, a row is added to the expense sheet.
Driver, vendor, date, total, tax, category and a link to the file, all in one row.
Finally, the driver gets a WhatsApp reply.
Tunde sees exactly what was logged, about a minute after sending it.
From a photo on WhatsApp to a filed, logged expense.
